title: Facade daemon protocol
description: The daemon protocol uses JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line: hello, call, watch, unwatch, and changed notifications. Clients skip unknown change kinds.

AgentCreator.description: The source of an agent's start, as displayed to the caller.

address.description: The agent's address in the requesting daemon's machine view.

resumable.description: The managed agent has a recorded session that Facade can resume.

AgentLabel.description: The identity and state of the reachable agent selected by an operation or offered as a match.

AgentListEntry.description: A roster row and the exact reference to use for later operations.

AgentListRow.description: A public roster row. The ID is the agent's copyable address.

AgentRef.description: An agent's durable identity, independently of names and routes.

AgentRemoval.description: The recorded cause of an agent record's removal.

watch.description: The watch number returned on this connection.

change.description: A change with the type defined by the watched topic.

cli.description:
The name a start gives: a built-in's, such as `claude`, or the name of a CLI the settings
file adds.

display_name.description: The name people know it by: a built-in's, such as `Claude Code`, or an added CLI's own.

available.description: Whether it can be started: its entry is right and its program is found.

problem.description:
Why it cannot be started: what is wrong with its entry, or that its program cannot run where
it would start, each said by its setting. Omitted where it can.

not_installed.description:
A built-in CLI whose entry has no problem and names no program of its own, and whose
program is not found where the start would run: not installed. Only with `available` false.
A client may leave it out of its list instead of showing it as one that cannot start.
Omitted otherwise.

overrides.description: Whether a start can choose its model and its effort (CLIS-1.4).

CliInfo.description: A CLI a start can run: an entry of Facade's settings file (CONFIGURATION-2.1).

env.description: The client's launch environment for a local query.

CliListArgs.description: Lists CLIs using the selected machine's launch environment and working folder.

oneOf.description:
A `facade` command, or a client that reads as one does, as `facade-mcp` does to learn where
its agent works.
`facade-mcp`, the MCP server of one agent's CLI. Its hello names the agent it acts for.

An editor window: the part of it that runs where its agents run. Its hello describes the
window, and it acts for the person.
The start of a symmetric daemon machine session over SSH.

ClientKind.description: The kind of client connecting to the daemon.

ConnectFailedParams.description: Foreground handshake failed after local authorization.

ConnectedParams.description: Connection verified on the foreground stream.

lines.description: How many of the log's last lines to read: 200 where absent, and at most 200.

The last lines of `core/logs/daemon.log`, oldest first, the home folder written as `~`.
Empty where there is no log.

oneOf.description: Typed into the recipient's terminal and submitted.
Returned by a snapshot of the recipient's `messages` topic.
A message to the person: delivered to one or more member windows' subscriptions.

status.description: `pending` while the message is being delivered, then `success` or `failure`.

reason.description: Why it was not delivered. Omitted unless it failed.

text_written.description: How much of the message reached the recipient's terminal.

enter_written.description:
Whether the Enter that submits it reached the recipient's terminal. Omitted when that is not
known: the recipient read the message while its typist was typing it, its typist did not say
by the deadline, what it typed was still queued then, or the daemon before a restart had
begun its paste.

deadline.description:
When a pending delivery fails if the message is not delivered by then. Omitted once it is
settled.

delivered_via.description: How the message was delivered. Omitted unless it was.

delivered_at.description: When the message was delivered. Omitted unless it was.

oneOf.description: The recipient ended, or its terminal stopped taking input, before the message was delivered.

A draft held the recipient's input until the deadline. A draft that is not the message's own
is never typed over.
A menu, login, or question of the recipient's CLI held its input until the deadline.

The recipient's input was not recognized as empty until the deadline: its screen did not
show it as its CLI's rule describes it.

The input was empty, but the deadline passed before a paste of the message, its Enter, and
its confirmation could fit.

Its paste began, but the recipient's CLI did not take the message before the deadline. A
paste its terminal had not taken whole by then still goes in, and no Enter follows it.
The recipient's CLI has no rule to read its input by, so Facade types no message into it.

DeliveryFailure.description: Why a message was not delivered.

oneOf.description: The message is being delivered, or waits for its guest's next turn.
The message was delivered.
The message was not delivered.

DeliveryStatus.description: The state of a message's delivery.

oneOf.description:
Neither service held the CLI's terminal, so it closed. A CLI that ignores hangup may still
be running.

EndReason.description: Why an exit has no code or signal.

code.description:
The JSON-RPC error code: -32700 for invalid JSON, -32600 for an invalid request, -32601 for
an unknown method, -32602 for invalid arguments, and -32000 for other failures.

message.description: A plain-language explanation of the error.

reason.description: The error reason for clients to inspect.

text_written.description: With `partial_input` for text: how much of the text reached the agent's terminal.

enter_written.description: With `partial_input` for text: whether its Enter reached the agent's terminal.

keys_sent.description: With `partial_input` for keys: how many keys reached the agent's terminal whole.

kept.description:
With `worktree.create`, or `agent.start` with a `worktree`, that failed after Git made part
or all of the worktree: what it made, which stays.

entry.description:
With a refused start or resume that an entry of the settings file caused - its program not
found, the entry turned off or wrong, or a model or effort the entry gives that its CLI cannot
take - the entry's name, such as `claude`. A client offers to open the settings file.

available_clis.description: CLIs that can start here when the requested CLI is not configured.

message_ref.description: The original kept message, where its delivery outcome is unknown.

record_removal.description: A confirmed reason the addressed agent record was removed.

candidates.description: Complete references that matched a name or machine ID prefix.

agents.description: Reachable matches or the reachable agent whose operation failed.

machines.description: Matching machines or the selected machine whose connection failed.

sessions.description: Saved sessions matching the requested ID.

ErrorData.description: Error details for clients to inspect.

protocol.description: The highest protocol version shared by the client and daemon.

machine.description: The answering daemon's introduction on a machine session.

agents.description: The number of agent records when `hello` runs. Watch `agents` to receive changes.

keeper.description:
The keeper holding the agents' terminals. Omitted while no keeper runs; the daemon starts
one for the first agent.

HelloResult.description: The result of `hello`: daemon details and supported topics and operations.

above.description: Rows hidden above the visible input.

below.description: Rows hidden below the visible input.

HiddenRows.description: Rows of a draft scrolled out of the CLI's input, as the CLI marks them.

oneOf.description: It exited with code 0.
Facade stopped it.
It exited with another code, or a signal ended it.

InboxMessage.description: A complete inbox message as the receiving MCP client reads it.

evidence.description:
What on the screen the state rests on, such as `the input frame at row 22 is empty`. Never
the draft's text.

mechanism.description: The layout the agent's CLI rule reads. Omitted without a rule.

hidden.description: Draft rows scrolled out of the input. Omitted unless the CLI marks such rows.

InputInfo.description: An agent's message input as its screen shows it now.

oneOf.description: A prompt row inside a frame of two rules.
A prompt row above a model line at the bottom of the screen.
An editor between two rules, with a cursor the CLI draws.
A box of bar rows above a border.
The last row that starts with the prompt.

InputMechanism.description: The layout a CLI's rule reads its input from.

oneOf.description: The CLI's input is drawn empty.
The CLI's input holds text, typed, pasted, or recalled.
A menu or question of the CLI's own is drawn in place of its input.
The screen does not show the input as the CLI's rule describes it.

InputState.description: How an agent's message input reads on its screen. A reading never means input may be typed.

KeeperInfo.description: The keeper holding the agents' terminals.

path.description: The folder it made, an absolute path.

Kept.description: What a worktree creation that failed partway made, which stays: its branch, its folder, or both.

LegacyWorkspaceArgs.description: One legacy workspace selector from the specified machine.

oneOf.description: A folder outside any Git checkout, or one inside a checkout that is not its root.
A repository's main checkout.
A linked worktree of a repository.

boot_id.description: Changes each time the daemon starts. Distinguishes concurrent uses of a machine ID.

ssh_cleans_processes.description: On Linux, whether the system clears this user's processes at the end of the SSH session.

MachineHello.description: The introduction on each side of a machine hello.

paths.description: Both conflicting connection paths, including their sources.

MachineIdentity.description: A machine's persistent identity and current display name.

MachineMessage.description: A frame from either direction of a machine session. A request without an ID is a notification.

MachineQueryArgs.description: Selects a machine for a query. An omitted selector uses the operation's default.

name.description: The machine whose saved connection was removed.

via.description: The next machine on a remaining indirect route, in the client's machine view.

MessageRef.description: A message's identity on the machine that assigned its number.

NoArgs.description: Empty arguments: `{}`. May be omitted for topics that take no arguments.

Notification.description: A message without an ID or response, such as `changed`.

Overrides.description: Whether a start can choose a CLI's model and its effort.

code.description:
The exit code, if the CLI exited normally and its status is known. On Windows every exit
has one: the process's 32-bit exit code carried as an `i32`, so that 0xC000013A is
-1073741510.

signal.description:
The terminating signal name, such as `SIGKILL`. Signal numbers vary by system. Never on
Windows.

reason.description:
Why no code or signal is available, if known. If all three fields are absent, the exit
status is unavailable.

at.description:
The exit time in UTC ISO 8601 format with milliseconds. For an exit without a code or
signal, the time Facade noticed it.

ProcessExit.description:
A recorded CLI exit. Without a code or signal, its status is unavailable; do not treat it as
exit code zero.

ProcessState.description: The reported process state of an agent.

PromptOutcome.description: A start prompt's message ID and what became of it.

next_cursor.description: Continue the page by passing this value as `after`.

oneOf.description: An argument is missing, malformed, or out of range, or the request is unsupported.
The agent, run, message, or watch does not exist.
The selected machine confirmed that the requested CLI session does not exist.
A reference names more than one agent, or the person and an agent: select one by its ID.
The agent ended: it takes no more input or messages.

A text or keys call stopped partway: the agent ended, or its terminal stopped taking input,
after part of the call reached the terminal. The error's data says what went in.

The operation cannot complete: for example, a stop or a screen watch's snapshot timed out,
or the keeper disconnected.

The two sides share no protocol version, or a required client kind, operation, or field is
unsupported.
Two running daemons introduced themselves with the same machine ID.
A saved SSH connection needs a foreground login or verification.

A message exceeds the line limit, or input exceeds the per-call limit or available queue
room.
An internal Facade error.

The caller is not allowed to perform this operation. The keeper accepts only the daemon
holding the daemon lock.

Facade's settings file, `facade.json` in the Facade home, cannot be read as it must, which
stops every launch until it is fixed. The message says each problem, with the file's path
and, where known, its line and column.

The call was withdrawn by its `cancel` before it took effect: a message whose paste had not
begun, which is not kept.
Git could not make a worktree it was asked for: `data.kept` says what it made, which stays.

A newer Facade is taking over: the call did nothing, and a client repeats it once the new
daemon answers.

The CLI cannot do what the call asks of it: take a model or an effort it has no way to set,
or resume a session that a CLI of another type had.

Reason.description: Error reasons shared by both protocols.

agent_id.description:
The stable ID is `a` followed by a number. It is unique within its Facade home while
that home's SQLite database (`core/facade.db`) retains the agent number counter.

address.description: The copyable address, including a machine selector. The serving daemon fills client views.

label.description: The label in the serving client's machine view.

unreachable.description: The running machine is currently unreachable.

name.description: The display name. Names are nonempty but may repeat.

cli.description:
The CLI: the name of its entry in Facade's settings file, a built-in's such as `claude` or
an added one such as `Codex · work` (CONFIGURATION-2.1), or the program's file name for a
program started by its path or name.

cwd.description: The CLI's working folder at startup.

machine_id.description: The ID of the Facade machine that runs the agent.

pid.description: The CLI's process ID. Omitted for a guest, whose process Facade does not know.

process.description: Whether the CLI is running or ended.

cols.description: Terminal width in columns. Omitted for a guest, which has no terminal of Facade's.

rows.description: Terminal height in rows. Omitted for a guest.

created_at.description: When the agent was first created, in UTC ISO 8601 format with milliseconds.

started_at.description: The latest start or resume time, in UTC ISO 8601 format with milliseconds.

creator.description: The agent whose client started it. Omitted where the person started it, and for a guest.

creator_machine_id.description: The creator's machine ID. Omitted when it is the record's own machine.

root.description:
The first agent of its creation tree: itself where it has no creator, or else its creator's
root. It stays when agents of the tree end or go.

root_machine_id.description: The root agent's machine ID. Omitted when it is the record's own machine.

yolo.description:
Whether its run has YOLO on: its CLI runs without asking, and it reaches every agent. With
YOLO off, its CLI runs as it natively does, and it reaches only the agents of its creation
tree. A launch takes it from Facade's settings file, `facade.json`, as it is accepted; a
guest as it joins.

exit.description: The recorded exit. Omitted while the agent is running.

session.description:
The ID of the CLI session the agent's CLI last reported, which `agent.resume` continues.
Omitted until one is reported.

state_detail.description:
More about the state: what the CLI waits for, its own words, how its process ended, or why
the state is unknown.

said.description: The last thing that went into the agent's message input. Omitted until something has.

tools_state.description: Whether the agent's CLI can use Facade's tools.

tools_reason.description: Why the agent's CLI cannot use Facade's tools. Omitted unless they are unavailable.

id.description:
A non-negative integer request ID, at most u64::MAX. Omit it for a notification. The
response repeats this ID.

method.description: The method name, such as `hello` or `call`.

Request.description: A method call. Calls with an ID receive a response; calls without an ID are notifications.

id.description: The request ID, or `null` for a malformed request.

result.description: The success result, with the type defined by the method or operation.

error.description: The error on failure. Omitted when the response contains a result.

Response.description: A response containing either a result or an error.

name.description: The name of a managed agent. Omitted for a saved session.

stopped.description: The managed run ended because Facade stopped it.

at.description: The managed run's exit time or the saved session's modification time.

from_saved_session.description: The call created a new agent to open a saved CLI session.

ResumeTarget.description: The copyable agent address or the CLI session and its working location.

text.description: The text on one line, at most 1,024 characters.

from.description: Who said it: an agent ID, or `human` for the person.

from_name.description: The agent's name when it said it. Omitted for the person.

at.description: When, in UTC ISO 8601 format with milliseconds.

Said.description:
What last went into an agent's message input with Enter: what the person submitted in its
terminal and its CLI took, text typed with `agent.type` and `enter`, or a message delivered
through the terminal.

oneOf.description: The normal screen, with scrollback.
The alternate screen, which a full-screen view draws on. It has no scrollback.

ScreenBuffer.description: The screen buffer a CLI shows.

data.description:
Standard base64 with padding. Decode to bytes and continue the viewer's terminal parser
with them.

oneOf.description: Base64-encoded terminal output with queries removed.

data.description: Standard base64 with padding. Decode to terminal bytes and apply at this redraw's size.

cols.description: Terminal width required to apply this redraw.

rows.description: Terminal height required to apply this redraw.

oneOf.description:
A full redraw after missed output, a resize, or a return to the main screen. Apply it at its
own size, which may differ from the snapshot.

exit_status.description: The shell exit status calculated on the machine that ran the agent, if known.

oneOf.description: The recorded exit of the agent.
The agent was removed. No changes follow on this watch.

ScreenChange.description:
A change to the `screen` topic. `exit` follows all output the CLI wrote before ending; processes
still holding its terminal may write afterward. On macOS, the terminal is taken from those
processes when the CLI ends. `removed` is the watch's last change. Skip unknown change kinds.

`snapshot.redraw`, `output.data`, and `redraw.data` contain standard base64 with padding. Decode
them to bytes and feed those bytes to the viewer's terminal parser. Set the viewer to
`snapshot.cols` by `snapshot.rows` before the initial redraw. Each redraw change carries its own
`cols` and `rows`; use that size before applying its `data`. Process changes for each watch in
arrival order. Apply `output` as continuation bytes; `redraw` supplies a replacement terminal
sequence. Preserve parser state between messages. Do not treat the decoded bytes as plain text;
use `agent.screen` for plain text.

ServerMessage.description: A response or notification received from a server.

SessionMatch.description: A saved session that matched the requested session ID.

command.description: The complete command and arguments with which to repair the saved connection.

kind.description: What the CLI waits for, on `waiting_for_you`.

text.description:
The CLI's own words where it gave any, on `waiting_for_you` and on an `error` the CLI
reported. Untrusted text on one line.

how.description:
How the process ended, on `ended`. Omitted when its exit status is unavailable and Facade
did not stop it; `exit.reason` says what is known.

reason.description:
Why nothing shows what the CLI is doing, on `unknown`, or what Facade found wrong, on an
`error` it found: a start that showed nothing, or tools the CLI cannot use.

oneOf.description: `unknown`: a program without a rule has shown nothing of what it is doing since it started.
`unknown`: the CLI asked to report what it is doing and has not reported since.

`unknown`: the CLI took back what it reported, or a full reset or a shell's new prompt ended
it.
`unknown`: the CLI's screen shows nothing its rule recognizes.

`error`: a CLI started by its rule's name showed nothing of what it is doing within 60
seconds of its start or resume.
`error`: the CLI cannot use the Facade tools it was given; `tools_reason` says why.

StateReason.description: Why nothing shows what an agent's CLI is doing, or what Facade found wrong with it.

TerminalColors.description:
The colors an editor window's terminals draw with, each `#rrggbb`. An agent of the window
replies to its CLI's OSC 10, 11 and 12 queries with them; a color left out gets no reply.

oneOf.description: None of it.
Part of it.
All of it.

Not known: the recipient read the message while its typist was typing it, its typist did not
say by the deadline, what it typed was still queued then, to reach the terminal once the CLI
reads, or the daemon before a restart had begun its paste.

TextWritten.description: How much of a message reached the recipient's terminal.

oneOf.description: Facade could not give them to this run's CLI; the daemon's log says why.

Its Facade server did not connect within 60 seconds of the run's start or resume, or of a
daemon's recovery of the run.

Its CLI starts its servers only with its first turn or its panel of servers, and the run's
start could not have the panel start Facade's server before the first turn; the daemon's log
says why. The first turn starts it.
Its Facade server's last connection closed while the run went on.
The CLI ended.

ToolsReason.description: Why an agent's CLI cannot use the Facade tools it was given.

oneOf.description: The CLI was not given the tools: it has no rule, or its rule does not give them.
The CLI was given the tools, and its server has not answered the CLI's `tools/list` yet.
The CLI's server answered its `tools/list` and holds a connection.
The CLI was given the tools but cannot use them; `tools_reason` says why.

ToolsState.description:
Whether an agent's CLI can use Facade's tools: `facade-mcp`, the MCP server that a CLI started
by its rule is given for its run.

agent.description: The target that took the input. Raw terminal input keeps the empty receipt.

matches.description: Complete addresses returned before a name lookup could finish.

watch.description: The watch number returned by `watch` on this connection.

program.description: The program, a `facade`, with its `facade-mcp` beside it.

build.description: Its build, as its `hello` says it.

daemon_protocol.description: The daemon protocol range accepted for this takeover, lowest and highest.

keeper_protocol.description: The keeper protocol versions it speaks, lowest and highest.

UpgradeArgs.description:
Arguments for `daemon.upgrade`: the program of a newer build that takes over, as the command
that asks runs it.

agents.description: The agents that keep running through the takeover: those whose run runs.

agent_id.description:
The stable ID is `a` followed by a number. It is unique within its Facade home while
that home's SQLite database (`core/facade.db`) retains the agent number counter.

address.description: The copyable address, including a machine selector. The serving daemon fills client views.

label.description: The label in the serving client's machine view.

unreachable.description: The running machine is currently unreachable.

name.description: The display name. Names are nonempty but may repeat.

cli.description:
The CLI: the name of its entry in Facade's settings file, a built-in's such as `claude` or
an added one such as `Codex · work` (CONFIGURATION-2.1), or the program's file name for a
program started by its path or name.

cwd.description: The CLI's working folder at startup.

machine_id.description: The ID of the Facade machine that runs the agent.

windows.description: One or more member windows, unique and sorted by machine ID and window ID.

location_id.description: The ID of its location: the location `cwd` is, or the innermost one that contains `cwd`.

location_source_window.description: The window that provided the agent's running location, where a window supplied it.

pid.description: The CLI's process ID. Omitted for a guest, whose process Facade does not know.

process.description: Whether the CLI is running or ended.

cols.description: Terminal width in columns. Omitted for a guest, which has no terminal of Facade's.

rows.description: Terminal height in rows. Omitted for a guest.

created_at.description: The start time in UTC ISO 8601 format with milliseconds.

creator.description: The agent whose client started it. Omitted where the person started it, and for a guest.

creator_machine_id.description: The creator's machine ID. Omitted when it is the record's own machine.

root.description:
The first agent of its creation tree: itself where it has no creator, or else its creator's
root. It stays when agents of the tree end or go.

root_machine_id.description: The root agent's machine ID. Omitted when it is the record's own machine.

yolo.description:
Whether its run has YOLO on: its CLI runs without asking, and it reaches every agent. With
YOLO off, its CLI runs as it natively does, and it reaches only the agents of its creation
tree. A launch takes it from Facade's settings file, `facade.json`, as it is accepted; a
guest as it joins.

exit.description: The recorded exit. Omitted while the agent is running.

session.description:
The ID of the CLI session the agent's CLI last reported, which `agent.resume` continues.
Omitted until one is reported.

state_detail.description:
More about the state: what the CLI waits for, its own words, how its process ended, or why
the state is unknown.

said.description: The last thing that went into the agent's message input. Omitted until something has.

tools_state.description: Whether the agent's CLI can use Facade's tools.

tools_reason.description: Why the agent's CLI cannot use Facade's tools. Omitted unless they are unavailable.

guest.description:
A guest: a session of a CLI the person started outside Facade, which joined through the
CLI's hooks. Its terminal is not Facade's: Facade cannot read its screen, type into it,
resize, stop or resume it. Omitted for an agent Facade started.

oneOf.description: The CLI has not shown what it is doing yet, within 60 seconds of its start or resume.
The CLI is working, or stopped working less than a second ago.

The CLI waits for the person; `state_detail.kind` says for what. A menu or question it draws
in place of its input counts, with `kind` `unknown` where it did not say, also while it
starts.

A turn ended while no terminal showed the agent. It stays so until one does. Work before the
CLI is asked to do anything is no turn: an Enter typed into it asks, unless it answers a
question the CLI shows. Words after the CLI's name at its start are the CLI's own and ask
nothing.
The CLI is not working and waits for nothing.

The CLI reported an error or its screen shows that the turn it reported ended failed, or,
started by its rule's name, it showed nothing of what it is doing within 60 seconds of its
start or resume.
The CLI's process ended; `state_detail.how` says how, where that is known.
Nothing shows what the CLI is doing; `state_detail.reason` says why.

V2AgentState.description:
What an agent is doing, from its CLI's own status reports, from its screen where its CLI's rule
reads it, and from Facade's own facts. The first state that holds, in this order, is the
agent's: `waiting_for_you`, `error`, `just_done`, `working`, `idle`, `starting`, then `unknown`;
`ended` once its process ended.

watch.description: The watch number returned on this connection.

change.description: A change with the type defined by the watched topic.

protocol.description: The oldest and newest daemon protocol versions the client supports.

kind.description: The client kind. Unsupported kinds are rejected at hello.

agent.description:
The agent this client acts for, by ID: the agent of `facade-mcp`, or the agent in whose
terminal a `facade` command runs. Messages the client sends come from that agent, and the
`messages` topic reads its inbox. Required for `mcp`, whose agent must be listed: a hello
naming one that is not is refused with `not_found`.

sessions.description:
The sessions the client's CLI names in its environment, such as `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`.
The client acts for the agent that has one of them, the newest where several do, ahead of
`agent`: a command a guest's model runs acts for the guest.

window.description:
The editor window this client is part of. Required for `ide`, and refused for any other
kind. Every connection of a window describes it; the window is there while one of them is
open.

numbers_given.description:
For an `ide` client: the highest agent and message numbers its editor gave before, such as 41
for `#a41`. The daemon's next numbers are above both these and its own, from then on.
Refused for any other kind with `invalid_argument`.

machine.description: Required on a machine session, absent on a local client connection.

protocol.description: The highest protocol version shared by the client and daemon.

machine.description: The answering daemon's introduction on a machine session.

window.description: For an `ide` client, the logical window bound to this connection.

agent.description:
The agent this client acts for, as `agent` and `sessions` decided. Omitted where it acts for
none.

agents.description: The number of agent records when `hello` runs. Watch `agents` to receive changes.

keeper.description:
The keeper holding the agents' terminals. Omitted while no keeper runs; the daemon starts
one for the first agent.

V2HelloResult.description: The result of `hello`: daemon details and supported topics and operations.

location_id.description:
`loc-` followed by 16 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the location's path: the same in
every window that lists it.

label.description: The checkout's branch, or else the folder's name.

path.description: The absolute path, with symbolic links resolved.

kind.description: What the location is: a folder, a repository's main checkout, or a linked worktree.

V2LocationInfo.description:
A place an agent can work: a window's folder, or a checkout of a Git repository one of its
folders is in.

machine_id.description: The other end of the connection.

V2MachineConnection.description: One connection as seen from its machine table row.

boot_id.description: The running daemon, where observed. Every advertised route carries it.

route.description:
The remaining hops, ending at this machine. Empty for the table's own machine.
Absent for a saved destination without a route.

V2MachineInfo.description: A row visible from the machine that supplies the table.

answered_at.description: The UTC time of the answer, to milliseconds, when a machine answered.

V2MachineQueryResult.description: The outcome of asking one machine for its reachable agents.

message_id.description: `m` followed by a number, unique within the Facade home.

message_ref.description: The full reference for a window notification to the person or a remote send receipt.

from.description:
The sender: an agent ID, `human` for the person, or `facade` for a result: Facade's own
words on what became of a start, not an agent's.

from_machine_id.description: The sender's machine, when different from the one that stored the message.

from_name.description: The sender's name when it sent the message. Omitted for the person.

to.description: The recipient's agent ID, or `human` for the person.

reply_to_machine_id.description: The replied-to message's machine, when different from the one that stored this message.

from_window.description:
The sender's window name if it had a single member window and the recipient did not belong
to that window.

call_id.description:
A result's call: the ID of the MCP `tools/call` it answers later. On a start's prompt, the
call its result answers.

result.description: A result's facts, which its text words. Omitted for any other message.

at.description: When Facade received it, in UTC ISO 8601 format with milliseconds.

V2Message.description: A message: one sender, one recipient, the complete text, and what became of it.

agent.description: The highest agent number, such as 41 for `#a41`; 0 for none. At most 2^53 - 1.

message.description: The highest message number, such as 230 for `#m230`; 0 for none. At most 2^53 - 1.

V2NumbersGiven.description: The highest numbers an editor gave before.

command.description:
The CLI followed by more of its arguments. The exact name of a CLI of Facade's settings
file, `facade.json` in the Facade home - a built-in's, such as `claude`, or one its `clis`
adds - starts that CLI as its entry says, its entry's `args` before these (CONFIGURATION-2,
3). Any other word, including a path, runs as that program, as given. A start from an `mcp`
client names one CLI of the file and nothing more; another name is refused with `not_found`,
naming the CLIs there. A file that cannot be read as a whole refuses every start with
`configuration_invalid`, and so does a CLI whose entry is wrong, saying each problem; a CLI
its entry turns off is refused with `unavailable`, and one whose program cannot run where it
starts with `not_found`, saying so by its setting.

name.description:
The display name, trimmed. A missing, empty, or blank name gets a name from the settings
file's `names`, else from the built-in names: one unused in any of the initial member
windows, ignoring case and surrounding spaces. If every name is taken or the list is empty,
uses the agent's ID, such as `#a7` (LIFECYCLE-2.1). Given names may repeat.

cwd.description:
The CLI's absolute working folder. If `location_source_window` is set, `cwd` must be that
window's location or a folder inside one.

machine.description: The machine selector at the entrance to a start. Omitted to use the caller's machine.

cwd_is_default.description: The caller supplied its default cwd. A remote start uses the running machine's login home.

window.description: The one initial member window, when supplied. Omitted to use the caller's default.

initial_windows.description: The initial members the originating daemon verified for a forwarded start.

location_source_window.description: The connected local window that supplies the running location for `cwd`, if selected.

env.description:
The environment supplied by the client. If omitted, the CLI gets only `TERM`, `COLORTERM`,
and `PWD`. It does not inherit the daemon's environment. Facade removes terminal, editor,
and CLI session variables, but keeps `TERM_PROGRAM` and `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION`, which tell
the CLI which terminal app displays it; then it sets `TERM`, `COLORTERM`, and `PWD`. Supply
the user's remaining environment explicitly. `facade start` does this, omitting non-UTF-8
variables and naming them on stderr. A start from an `mcp` client takes its agent's
environment instead, as that agent's CLI started with it, less what that CLI's rule added: a
CLI chooses what it gives its MCP server, while a `facade` command sends its shell's. Where
that environment cannot be read, as when the CLI is not running or the system hides it, the
start fails with `unavailable` and starts nothing. A start that an agent asks for, from its
tools or its terminal, inherits that environment as it is, including what the agent's own
entry `env` set or removed, as a shell started from another inherits its variables; the
started CLI's own entry applies on top (CONFIGURATION-2.1, 3.2).

cols.description: The initial terminal width in columns, at least 2.

rows.description: The initial terminal height in rows, at least 1.

prompt.description:
The agent's first message, its text as `agent.send` takes it: from the agent the client acts
for, or else from the person. It is kept as the start answers, and delivered once the CLI's
tools connected or will not, before any other message. A prompt from an agent owes that
agent a result once it is settled. Only a CLI of the settings file takes one: a program
started by its path or name is refused one, and the program of a `custom` entry, whose input
Facade does not read, starts and fails it as `unsupported` (CONFIGURATION-2.3).

call_id.description: The ID of the MCP `tools/call` that asked for the start, which the prompt's result names.

result_message_id.description: The creator's reserved result message number for a forwarded start with a prompt.

result_message_machine_id.description: The machine that reserved the result message number.

request_id.description:
The caller's own ID of this start, 1 to 200 characters. The same ID again from the same
creator, including its machine, and target within an hour answers that agent as it stands, and starts
nothing. A start that failed keeps none, and the ID goes with its agent's record.

worktree.description:
A worktree with a new branch to make and start in. With a location source window, uses
the supplied location. Otherwise, uses the repository of `cwd`. The daemon checks the
request ID before it makes the worktree, so a repeat makes none.

model.description:
The model this start chooses, over its entry's `model` (CONFIGURATION-3.3, CLIS-1.4). A CLI
that takes none from Facade, as OpenCode and a program do not, refuses it with
`unsupported`. Omitted, a model the command's own words choose, else the entry's, else the
CLI's own.

effort.description: The effort this start chooses, over its entry's `effort`, as `model` is.

session.description:
A session of the CLI to continue, as `agent.resume` continues one: the CLI's rule gives the
arguments that continue it, the same way for every CLI. The start is a new agent, with its own
number. A CLI whose rule does not resume sessions, and a program that is not a CLI of the
settings file, refuse it with `unsupported` before anything starts. Refused from an `mcp`
client, as more words are.

V2StartArgs.description: Arguments for `agent.start`, supplied by the client.

agent.description: The started agent as it was when its prompt was settled.

V2StartOutcome.description: What became of a start with a prompt, as its result tells the agent that started it.

prompt.description: The prompt, kept and pending, where one was given.

result_message_id.description:
The ID of the result the prompt owes the agent the client acts for, a message from `facade`
once the prompt is settled. Omitted where no result is owed.

result_message_machine_id.description: The machine that assigned `result_message_id`, when a result is owed.

repeated.description:
The call repeated an earlier one by its request ID: the agent is that call's, as it stands
now. Omitted otherwise.

watch.description: The watch number used by `changed` notifications and `unwatch`.

snapshot.description: The topic snapshot. Later changes arrive as ordered `changed` notifications.

V2WatchResult.description: The result of `watch`, sent before any changes for that watch.

id.description:
The editor window instance's ID. It survives reloads and changes when the window reopens.
The daemon returns the logical window in `HelloResult.window`.

environment.description:
`local`, or the remote authority, such as `ssh-remote+devbox`, of a window whose user
interface is on another computer.

workspace.description:
A workspace the daemon can use to bind a reopened window to an earlier logical window.
Omitted for a window with no workspace.

folders.description:
The window's folders, as absolute paths, in the editor's order. Each is a location, and so
is every checkout of a Git repository one of them is in.

branch_prefix.description:
The window's Git branch prefix, which a new worktree's folder name leaves out. Omitted where
none is set.

colors.description:
The colors the window supplies for its agents' terminal color queries. `window.update`
sends them again when the editor's theme changes. An omitted color gets no reply.

env.description:
The environment the window's agents start with, as the editor works it out for its first
folder's terminals. Facade looks for each CLI's program on its `PATH` to say in `clis` which
can start. Omitted, the window lists neither `clis` nor `settings_problem` to an `ide` client.

V2WindowDescription.description:
An editor window as it describes itself, in `hello` and again with `window.update` whenever any
of it changes.

machine_id.description: The ID of the Facade machine that owns the window.

environment.description:
`local`, or the remote authority of an editor window whose user interface is on another
computer.

connected.description:
Whether the logical window has a current connection. The terminal window always reports
connected.

folders.description: The window's folders, in its order. The terminal window has none.

locations.description:
Where an agent of the window can start: each folder and Git checkout once, a repository's
main checkout first. The terminal window's are the folders its running agents work in.

problems.description: What Facade could not read of the window's locations, which are then as last read.

observed_at.description:
When Facade last read the window's locations, in UTC ISO 8601 format with milliseconds; for
the terminal window, when it was listed. Omitted for a window whose locations this daemon
has not read yet.

clis.description:
The CLIs a start can run in this window, each found on a `PATH` or not: for a client that
acts for an agent, that agent's; for an `ide` client, the one in the window's own `env`.
None for a window with no folder, and none where Facade's settings file cannot be read as a
whole. Omitted for a client that acts for no agent, and for an `ide` client where the window
gave no `env`.

settings_problem.description:
For a client that acts for an agent, or an `ide` client where the window gave `env`, what is
wrong with Facade's settings file where it cannot be read as a whole, which then lists no
CLI and stops every start, as one text. Omitted where the file reads.

V2WindowInfo.description:
A window: an editor window, or the terminal window, `terminal`, which holds the agents started
from a terminal.

machine_id.description: The Facade machine's ID, a lowercase UUID version 4.

window_id.description: The logical window's ID, or `terminal` for that machine's terminal window.

V2WindowRef.description: A logical window on a Facade machine.

oneOf.description: Insert or replace the window by its machine ID and logical window ID.
Remove the logical window identified by both fields.

branch.description: The new branch, which must not exist yet.

base_ref.description: The commit the branch starts from, as Git reads it: `HEAD`, a branch, a tag, or a commit.

V2Worktree.description: A new worktree: its branch and where the branch starts.

agent_id.description:
The stable ID is `a` followed by a number. It is unique within its Facade home while
that home's SQLite database (`core/facade.db`) retains the agent number counter.

address.description: The copyable address, including a machine selector. The serving daemon fills client views.

label.description: The label in the serving client's machine view.

unreachable.description: The running machine is currently unreachable.

name.description: The display name. Names are nonempty but may repeat.

cli.description:
The CLI: the name of its entry in Facade's settings file, a built-in's such as `claude` or
an added one such as `Codex · work` (CONFIGURATION-2.1), or the program's file name for a
program started by its path or name.

cwd.description: The CLI's working folder at startup.

machine_id.description: The ID of the Facade machine that runs the agent.

pid.description: The CLI's process ID. Omitted for a guest, whose process Facade does not know.

process.description: Whether the CLI is running or ended.

cols.description: Terminal width in columns. Omitted for a guest, which has no terminal of Facade's.

rows.description: Terminal height in rows. Omitted for a guest.

created_at.description: When the agent was first created, in UTC ISO 8601 format with milliseconds.

started_at.description: The latest start or resume time, in UTC ISO 8601 format with milliseconds.

creator.description: The agent whose client started it. Omitted where the person started it, and for a guest.

creator_machine_id.description: The creator's machine ID. Omitted when it is the record's own machine.

root.description:
The first agent of its creation tree: itself where it has no creator, or else its creator's
root. It stays when agents of the tree end or go.

root_machine_id.description: The root agent's machine ID. Omitted when it is the record's own machine.

yolo.description:
Whether its run has YOLO on: its CLI runs without asking, and it reaches every agent. With
YOLO off, its CLI runs as it natively does, and it reaches only the agents of its creation
tree. A launch takes it from Facade's settings file, `facade.json`, as it is accepted; a
guest as it joins.

exit.description: The recorded exit. Omitted while the agent is running.

session.description:
The ID of the CLI session the agent's CLI last reported, which `agent.resume` continues.
Omitted until one is reported.

state_detail.description:
More about the state: what the CLI waits for, its own words, how its process ended, or why
the state is unknown.

said.description: The last thing that went into the agent's message input. Omitted until something has.

tools_state.description: Whether the agent's CLI can use Facade's tools.

tools_reason.description: Why the agent's CLI cannot use Facade's tools. Omitted unless they are unavailable.

agents.description: For a synced machine, its complete records, including an empty list.

oneOf.description: The CLI has not shown what it is doing yet, within 60 seconds of its start or resume.
The CLI is working, or stopped working less than a second ago.

The CLI waits for the person; `state_detail.kind` says for what. A menu or question it draws
in place of its input counts, with `kind` `unknown` where it did not say, also while it
starts.

A turn ended while no terminal showed the agent. It stays so until one does. Work before the
CLI is asked to do anything is no turn: an Enter typed into it asks, unless it answers a
question the CLI shows. Words after the CLI's name at its start are the CLI's own and ask
nothing.
The CLI is not working and waits for nothing.

The CLI reported an error or its screen shows that the turn it reported ended failed, or,
started by its rule's name, it showed nothing of what it is doing within 60 seconds of its
start or resume.
The CLI's process ended; `state_detail.how` says how, where that is known.
Nothing shows what the CLI is doing; `state_detail.reason` says why.
A Guest is connected and can take messages.
Insert or replace the whole agent record by machine and agent ID.
Remove the record with this machine and agent ID.
The state of this running machine's contribution to the view.

agents.description: Records on the machine that serves this view.

V3Caller.description: An identity verified by the daemon that accepted the original request.

V3DeliverStartResultArgs.description: A start outcome with the message number already reserved on the recipient's machine.

recipient.description: The resolved destination of `agent.send`, used again on retry.

V3ForwardCall.description: A forwarded call and the facts verified by the originating machine.

route.description: Remaining machine IDs, from this hop's receiver to the destination.

V3ForwardParams.description: Parameters of `forward`. The outer JSON-RPC ID identifies this hop.

V3HelloParams.description: Introduces a daemon client or a machine. Actor identity is supplied by the daemon.

rule.description:
The CLI rule the agent was started by: its CLI's name, such as `claude`. Omitted for an
agent started by a program path or a name without a rule.

session_tracking.description: Whether the running CLI reports its session to Facade. False for an ended agent.

started_by.description: The recorded startup source, where it is known.

viewers.description: The viewers currently attached to the terminal.

attachments.description: The verified client kinds and originating machines of those attachments.

launch_command.description:
The actual launch command formatted by the running machine, with run credentials redacted.
Omitted if this run's launch command was not recorded.

location_id.description:
`loc-` followed by 16 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the location's path: the same in
every window that lists it.

label.description: The checkout's branch, or else the folder's name.

path.description: The absolute path, with symbolic links resolved.

kind.description: What the location is: a folder, a repository's main checkout, or a linked worktree.

source_folder.description: The requested workspace folder that produced this local result.

machine_id.description: The other end of the connection.

boot_id.description: The running daemon, where observed. Every advertised route carries it.

route.description:
The remaining hops, ending at this machine. Empty for the table's own machine.
Absent for a saved destination without a route.

status.description: Whether this query obtained the machine's contribution.

error.description: The reason this query failed, when known.

oneOf.description: A temporary channel supplied by the client, such as an editor's existing SSH connection.

message_id.description: `m` followed by a number, unique within the Facade home.

message_ref.description: The full reference, when a remote message receipt needs it.

from.description: The sender: an agent ID, `command_line` or `facade`.

from_machine_id.description: The sender's machine, when different from the one that stored the message.

from_name.description: The sender's name when it sent the message. Omitted for `command_line` and `facade`.

reply_to_machine_id.description: The replied-to message's machine, when different from the one that stored this message.

call_id.description:
A result's call: the ID of the MCP `tools/call` it answers later. On a start's prompt, the
call its result answers.

result.description: A result's facts, which its text words. Omitted for any other message.

at.description: When Facade received it, in UTC ISO 8601 format with milliseconds.

name.description:
The new name, trimmed. An empty or blank name gets a default name chosen from the suggested
names: unused while one is available, otherwise reused. Names may repeat.

cols.description: Terminal width in columns, at least 2.

rows.description: Terminal height in rows, at least 1.

machine_id.description: The exact machine saved with a Pin. Mutually exclusive with the public machine selector.

V3ResumeArgs.description: The copyable agent address or the CLI session and its working location.

lines.description: The number of lines to return, from 1 to 2000. Defaults to 50.

agent_id.description: The ID of the agent being viewed.

machine_id.description: The agent's running machine, for reconnecting to its exact reference.

cols.description: Terminal width required to apply the redraw.

rows.description: Terminal height required to apply the redraw.

redraw.description:
Base64-encoded terminal bytes that redraw the screen at this size. Restores cursor state,
charsets, and modes. On the main screen, up to 1,000 rows of agent scrollback come first
unless `include_scrollback` is false. `keep_scrollback` controls whether the viewer's
existing scrollback is cleared before the redraw.

exit.description: The recorded exit, if the agent has ended.

exit_status.description: The shell exit status calculated on the machine that ran the agent, if known.

process.description: The agent's process state captured with this snapshot.
Whether the agent's CLI is running. An ended agent's screen is the one it left.

observed_at.description:
When the screen was read, in UTC ISO 8601 format with milliseconds; for an ended agent, when
it ended, as its screen is the one it left.

text.description:
The lines, joined by line feeds, each wrapped row joined into its line. Inverse text is
between `[[` and `]]` and dim text between `{{` and `}}`, inverse outside dim. Each
backslash, bracket, and brace of the screen's own text is escaped with a backslash, so
removing the marks and the escapes gives the text exactly; see [`crate::daemon::plain`].

older_lines.description: Whether output lies above the lines read.

trimmed.description: Whether the scrollback let go of its oldest lines.

keep_scrollback.description:
Keep the viewer's existing scrollback. Defaults to false: every snapshot and redraw clears
it first. A main-screen snapshot then replays up to 1,000 rows of the agent's scrollback
unless `include_scrollback` is false. Later redraws include only the visible screen.
`facade attach` sets this option to true.

include_scrollback.description:
Include up to 1,000 main-screen scrollback rows before the visible screen in the snapshot.
Defaults to true. `facade attach` sets it to false on reconnect so the viewer does not
receive those rows twice.

allow_ended.description: With an exact managed reference, allow the final snapshot of an ended run.

text.description:
The complete message: at most 8,000 characters and 540 lines of text, tabs, and line breaks,
not blank.

reply_to.description: The message this one answers, by ID or address such as `m4@gpu`.

reply_to_machine_id.description: The storage machine of the reply's reference, after the originating daemon verified it.

request_id.description:
The caller's own ID of this send, 1 to 200 characters. A retry within an hour with the same
sender, sender machine, target, and ID joins its ongoing delivery or returns its original
result. A withdrawn message keeps only a private record of the outcome for retries.

time_left_ms.description:
What is left of the send's 30 seconds as it leaves the client, in milliseconds: its
delivery's deadline counts that from the daemon's receipt, at most 29,500. Omitted, 29,500.

allow_unsupported_receipt.description: A terminal can request a numbered delivery outcome for a target without an input rule.

recipient.description: The recipient selected for this send, including when delivery fails.

expected_reply_to.description:
The original message the Guest was waiting for this sender to answer. It can be
included when a send without `reply_to` timed out and was withdrawn.

V3SendResult.description: The receipt of a send, with the address that can be used to wait for a reply.

folder_is_default.description: The entry's default folder, which is discarded when forwarding to another machine.

worktree.description: A branch to create as a worktree from the repository's current HEAD.

V3StartArgs.description: Shared arguments for start and preflight.

agent.description: The started agent as it was when its prompt was settled.

prompt.description: The prompt, kept and pending, where one was given.

result_message_id.description:
The ID of the result the prompt owes the agent the client acts for, a message from `facade`
once the prompt is settled. Omitted where no result is owed.

result_message_machine_id.description: The machine that assigned `result_message_id`, when a result is owed.

repeated.description:
The call repeated an earlier one by its request ID: the agent is that call's, as it stands
now. Omitted otherwise.

agent.description: The record whose run this call stopped.

code.description:
The exit code, if the CLI exited normally and its status is known. On Windows every exit
has one: the process's 32-bit exit code carried as an `i32`, so that 0xC000013A is
-1073741510.

signal.description:
The terminating signal name, such as `SIGKILL`. Signal numbers vary by system. Never on
Windows.

reason.description:
Why no code or signal is available, if known. If all three fields are absent, the exit
status is unavailable.

at.description:
The exit time in UTC ISO 8601 format with milliseconds. For an exit without a code or
signal, the time Facade noticed it.

already_ended.description: The CLI had ended before this stop, so the stop signaled nothing. Omitted when false.

V3StopResult.description:
A recorded CLI exit. Without a code or signal, its status is unavailable; do not treat it as
exit code zero.

raw.description:
Bytes from an attached terminal, encoded as standard base64 with padding. They are queued as
they are, also between a typed text and its Enter.

text.description:
Text to paste as one input: printable characters, tabs, and line breaks. When the CLI turned
on bracketed paste, the text goes between the paste brackets with each line break as a
carriage return; otherwise it goes as given.

enter.description:
Press Enter after `text`, in a write of its own 0.1 seconds and the CLI's settle time for
the text after the whole text reached the terminal. Empty text with `enter` presses Enter
alone. Defaults to false.

keys.description:
Keys to press in order: Enter (or Return), Escape (or Esc), Tab, Shift+Tab, Backspace,
Delete, Up, Down, Left, Right (or ArrowUp, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight), Home, End,
PageUp, PageDown, Space, and Ctrl+A to Ctrl+Z, in any letter case, or any one character
other than a control character, exactly as given. Each goes as a terminal sends it in the
CLI's modes. After an Escape, the next key waits 50 ms.

oneOf.description: The person's permission to go on.
The person's answer to a question.
The person to sign in.
The CLI did not say.

WatchEndedParams.description: A forwarded watch ended. A new watch starts with a fresh snapshot.

watch.description: The watch number used by `changed` notifications and `unwatch`.

snapshot.description: The topic snapshot. Later changes arrive as ordered `changed` notifications.

WatchResult.description: The result of `watch`, sent before any changes for that watch.
